title: Nine Minutes of Mending
subtitle: 钟表与计时 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 钟表与计时（生活与学习·时间与器物）
meta: 主题语境：钟表与计时（生活与学习·时间与器物）　|　核心词汇：clock　|　正文 335 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 clock 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1948 my mother was sent to mend ① clock she could not wind, and she said the mending was the whole of the lesson. The ② clock, meaning the machine and not the hour, was nine minutes slow and was mended by whoever came last; clock, she said, is the only thing in a hall that is judged by how much has been taken out of it.

Every ③ clock in that hall had the same face, and the ④ clock at the end, meaning the one the keeper kept and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever mended properly. Clock, my grandmother said, is nine parts patience and one part somebody willing to stay behind; my mother said the patience is the part that gets everywhere.

My father meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ clock was the whole of the shift, meaning the hour it carried and not the machine. The ⑥ clock, meaning the hour and not any of that, is the only thing in a shift that everybody watches and nobody questions; clock, he said, is either something you mend or the only word that means both a machine and an hour. She said the hour is the part they remember.

By 1963 the ⑦ clock had become a number in a report, and the report had become an argument about the face. The ⑧ clock of the whole thing, my mother wrote in April, was nine minutes and eleven years of mending; clock, she said, is either the one at the end or the reason you learned to stand on a chair. He said the chair was never mentioned.

The ⑨ clock I remember is the one at the end, which was mended in 1968 and is still described as the loudest in the county. A ⑩ clock, my grandmother said in 1973, is the only thing that improves by being mended; every clock, she said, is an hour that has agreed to look like a machine. She said the hour was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: B. n. 钟（指那台机器本身，与那个钟点相对）
C. 固定搭配：mend a clock 修一口钟
D. n. 钟（指那座大厅里每一口）
E. n. 钟（指末尾那一口）
F. n. 工时（抽象：它记下的那个钟点）
G. n. 那个钟点（抽象：那件事本身）
H. n. 权衡；整件事的分量（抽象总称）

items.q: The clock, meaning the machine and not the hour
clock was the whole of the shift
the clock had become a number in a report
The clock of the whole thing
A clock, my grandmother said in 1973

answers.why: mend a clock 意为“修一口钟”，1948 年母亲被派去修她上不动弦的那口钟。
clock 意为“钟、时钟”，指那台机器本身而不是那个钟点，慢了九分钟，由最后来的人修。
clock 指那座大厅里每一口钟，每一口都是同样的钟面。
clock 指末尾那一口（管理员保留的那一口），是唯一有人认真修过的。
clock 意为“工时”，抽象指它记下的那个钟点，父亲说 clock 就是那一班的全部。
clock 为抽象用法，指那个钟点本身，是一班岗里人人都盯、却没人质疑的东西。
clock 意为“钟、时钟”，到 1963 年这口 clock 成了报告里的一个数字。
clock 意为“权衡、整件事的分量”，母亲四月写道，整件事权衡下来是九分钟和十一年的修理。
clock 意为“钟”，我记得的是末尾那一口，1968 年修过，至今仍被说成全县最响的。
clock 为抽象总称，祖母说一口钟是唯一会因为被认真修理而变好的东西。
